sections.text: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम्।
The ignorant do not see that it is He Who is present in life and Who departs at death or even that it is He Who enjoys pleasure through the Qualities. Only the eye of wisdom sees.
The saints with great effort find Him within themselves; but not the unintelligent, who in spite of every effort cannot control their minds.
Remember that the Light which, proceeding from the sun, illumines the whole world, and the Light which is in the moon, and That which is in the fire also, all are born of Me.

We had been discussing chapter 15, Purushottam yoga, yoga of the Supreme Spirit, the Supreme Purusha. We have talked about Prakriti. The Prakriti has three aspects, the Sattva, rajas and Tamas. And this permutation combination of the Sattva, Rajas and Tamas create this multiplicity in this world. When we associate with it, it creates a sansar I in the world. In that relationship, we get lost.
And that relationship creates either the conducive experience or not conducive experience. Some gives us joy and some gives us unhappiness. So thats our Sansar. In that Sansar, we try to understand through various ways, to understand what gives me happiness, how can I achieve the permanent happiness. So, as we have seen before, our entire life is divided into two pursuits. One is to achieve happiness and other is to avoid unhappiness.
So this chapter starts with saying, well, lets understand how your Sansar starts. In the first place, place, it seems like it is rooted here, but its source is up above. Up above, in other sense, theres something which is beyond my perception, something which is beyond my understanding. From that source, this sansar grows and it is nourished by the Veda, the leaves and branches. The more I know about this sansar, more it grows, more I know about any subject, it becomes more and more complex. And even though my knowledge grows, my insecurity increases.
That there may be even a lot more that I do not know. The more we know about the atom, the less we know about the reality of what the atom actually is. In physics, when knowledge was limited, people could say, Well, I have understood everything and there is nothing more to be known. But the more we know, the more complex it becomes. This Sansaar is like that. This Sansaar is the theme of all scriptural advice and practices.
So this chapter tries to make this very clear to us: remaining in the Sansaar, getting attached to the Sansaar, will never give us what we seek. So the very first advice in this chapter says, with the strong axe of detachment, cut this tree of Sansaar. Detach yourself from this Sansaar. This is the only way to achieve that permanent happiness which you are seeking. And then we have discussed what is the nature of that self.
If I detach from this sensa, what am I getting attached to? You are getting attached to that supreme self. Having gone there, non returns. Once you have achieved that identification, there wont be any delusion. You will never come back to this ignorance. So as we had seen before, this Maya is created out of ignorance.
Maya is called Maya because it gives an appearance of something that which is not. I always give the example of David Copperfield, and I thought he must have disappeared somewhere. But he was in the news a few days ago. He was in a courtroom explaining how the illusion works. So this is the first time he has had to give the secret out in open court -- how he does that illusion -- because somebody got hurt. So it is an illusion.
But till we know how it happens, its a mystery for us. So this Sansaar is like that illusion -- even though it seems so real, we all come to understand from the scriptures that it is an illusion. It is the Maya, and we want to get out of this illusion. Once we understand, then anytime David Copperfield performs his act, we will not be in much confusion. We know whats happening there. If you have that vision of both at the same time, youve got it made.
So therefore, the one who understands both -- one who can see this Sansaar and the source of Sansaar -- he knows what the reality is. To get out of this ignorance in which we think this Sansaar is so real, you have to develop some mental capabilities. And we have seen those qualities: Nirmana moha, Jita sanga dosha.
One who is beyond the pride and whatever the opposite of that. And also jita sangha do saha who has a victory over attachment. We are trying to achieve that. But then we also want to understand what is the nature of myself. Then what is it that now considers that I as I am? And what is the relationship between the supreme self?
So we have learned that Mama Evamsha Jiva Loke Jiva Bhutah. The world of individual beings, where each one considers himself or herself to be an individual. We all consider ourselves to be a very complete individual, independent of each other. Thats our general understanding. We think that I am by myself and the world is out there to compete with me. Its actually the other way around.
I am there because the world is there. But thats never clear in our mind. So when one makes the connections, theres an all-pervading supreme self which acts as the source of all beings. When it comes to me as the individual, only a portion of that self associates with this mind and intellect. It basically, as we have seen, draws the five senses and mind from the Prakriti.
So everything that I consider myself right now belongs to the Prakriti. My mind, my intellect, my body. And we have seen previously in detail how this works. That the body is made of the grossified element. The five elements which has come into it gross forms. So you can identify them as five different elements.
And also we know where it comes from and where it goes. We know that the body is made of food. Its very simple for us to really follow this food chain. When I digested, it became my body. When I die, the same body will become food for somebody else. And the cycle continues.
What is not simple for us is to understand the subtle body. We always thought that my consciousness, my mind and my intellect are the thinkers who think. So we consider that as our real self, which is driving this body to do what it does. The distinction made here is that those are also part of the Prakriti, the inert nature. Nature is inert in all forms. It becomes sentient by association with the consciousness.
Just like we know for sure that my eye cannot see. I know now very much. I know more about eye than Im supposed to know. You know it basically no different than my glasses. So at least previously I had a Gods given lens inside. Now I have both acrylic lenses on both sides and they are shifted.
The guy said, dont worry about it. So it is no different than any other thing which breaks down in my house, my clothes or whatever. You can repair it and make it good again. So this body, mind and intellect are from this inert world. It becomes sentient only when it is associated with the consciousness. As long as I am aware, my eye can see.
And I am not aware of whats happening around my eye cannot see. We are seeing but not registering that what is there. Or we are hearing but not listening. Because the mind is not there. And the mind itself also cannot do anything, because it is made up of inert material.
Vedanta says that before these five elements were grossified, those five elements existed in their primordial state, which they call tanmatra. From these tanmatras, the mind and intellect are made. Those are still inert equipment, just like our body. But when the consciousness shines on that mind and intellect, then mind and intellect become capable of interpreting the experience which is happening. Only when consciousness is present and aware can I see and can my mind interpret -- even when I am alive. But when I am in deep sleep, the mind and intellect are in a dormant state because consciousness is not available to them.
Therefore the mind cannot interpret any experience in deep sleep. Therefore I wake up and say I dont know what happened. That I dont know and I know is my entire world. So the avidya is the root cause of my confusion about who I am. Avidya is part of Maya. So that avidya -- I dont know -- will associate with the Purusha, which is all knowledge.
That portion of me comes to say I know. And that I know creates the notion that I, the individual, know. So now I have created an entity called jiva. That jiva -- the consciousness identifying with the mind and intellect, considering itself to be an entity by itself, which is capable of knowing. So that jiva, when associated with the atma, which is the pure consciousness, is called jivatma. Mind and intellect identifying itself as an entity, associating with the consciousness, creates jivatma.
This jivatma remains intact as long as the conditionings are there. The standard example: the room space. The space was always here. But this very fact that space was here attracted somebody to build a building. Some developer who has an idea to create a building sees this space and says, I can build a building here. So this space, by its very existence, attracted walls and floor and ceiling into this space. Now it has created a room space -- now its the conditioned space.
So as long as this conditioning remains, the room space remains. This mind and intellect, once they come in association with the consciousness, identify with the limited consciousness which is reflecting through them and become a jivatma. This jivatma experiences this world through those five senses and the mind. Then we have seen that when this self leaves this body, one thing is sure -- we have seen people dying. So it follows that I will die too.
So what happens at the time of death is always a mystery to us. Bhagavan clarifies here that what happens here is that jivatma will leave this body carrying the fragrance with it off all the experiences and tendencies, all the fragrance of the mind and intellect which it has experienced through the senses, it will go with it. So Atmabodha actually describes the subtle body. What dies is only the gross body. The subtle body leaves as jivatma because it is constantly identifying with the consciousness which is all-pervading. Its like a mobile home or a car.
The space inside the car is identified with the car, but its not actually different from the space outside. It can move from here to Hanover County, and still the car space remains -- it moved from Germany to the United States, and its still the same car space. But now we know from our overall perspective, its not the same space when it is here versus there. If the space belonged to Henrico, its the space belonging to Henrico; if in Hanover, it belongs to Hanover. But because the conditioning is moving, and the space is omnipresent.
Wherever the conditioning moves, the identification moves with it. This jivatma associating with all pervading consciousness. When it moves from one body to another, it still identifies itself as an entity that is called a subtle body living so. So subtle body is the only thing which survives my death. And that subtle body is described in atma bodha. There are 17 elements: five pranas, ten senses -- pancha prana, dasha indriya -- thats 15.
Then mind and intellect make 17. These 17 remain as a subtle body -- not exactly the way we understand today. So not my physical eye is going to go, but the capacity and ability to remember that experience will go along with it, and that will then start its journey again. When I look at this experience, I think that when I die, my existence will end. So the verses we have seen say: Utkramantam sthitam va api bhunjanam va gunanvitam, vimudha na anupashyanti, pashyanti gnana chakshushah.

These verses draw a stark contrast between the deluded and the wise. The ignorant (vimudha) do not perceive the Self even as it departs at death, dwells in the body, or enjoys experiences through the gunas. Like watching a magic show without understanding the mechanism, we remain mystified by lifes appearances. But those with the eye of knowledge (jnana-chakshusah) see the truth. The yogis who strive with purified minds perceive the Self established within themselves, while those with unprepared minds, despite their efforts, cannot perceive it. Ask yourself honestly: am I striving with a prepared mind, or am I expecting results without the inner work?
Verse 12 offers a magnificent contemplation: the light of the sun that illumines the whole world, the light in the moon, the light in fire - all proceed from the Supreme. This is not poetic metaphor but a profound teaching about the nature of reality. Every light you see is borrowed light, reflecting that one original consciousness. Practice this today: when you see sunlight streaming through a window, when you notice moonlight, when you see a flame - pause and remember tat tejo viddhi mamakam - know that brilliance to be Mine. Let every source of illumination become a reminder that your own awareness, which makes all perception possible, is that same divine light manifesting through you.
